title: Hume AI MCP: How to Build a Voice Agent
summary: Hume AI MCP integration allows developers to link emotional intelligence directly to local databases and custom tools for context-aware responses.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions about Hume AI and MCP


### Can Hume AI use any MCP server?


Provided the server is hosted on a publicly accessible endpoint or within a reachable VPC, Hume AI can interface with any standards-compliant MCP server.


This compatibility allows the Empathetic Voice Interface (EVI) to call functions from a GitHub repository for codebase analysis or a PostgreSQL database for inventory lookups.


Every new server connection introduces a potential data egress point. You must audit the specific tools exposed by the server to prevent the model from accessing sensitive tables or restricted directories.


### Does using MCP increase the cost of Hume API calls?


Integrating MCP increases the total cost of an interaction because the retrieved context adds to the token count processed by the underlying language model.


While the Hume EVI itself maintains its base processing fee, the external calls to a knowledge base or a CRM like HubSpot consume additional compute resources and API credits.


You must monitor these overheads closely. A reactive agent that pulls long histories for every query will deplete its budget faster than one using filtered, targeted data fetches.


### Is Hume AI MCP compatible with Claude or ChatGPT?


Because Hume AI acts as the orchestration layer that can utilize models like Claude Sonnet 5.5 or GPT-6.2 Astra via its modular architecture, it is compatible with their respective MCP implementations.


This setup allows the system to pair Hume’s prosody analysis with the high-reasoning capabilities of Claude Opus 5.5 for complex troubleshooting.


The following data illustrates the rapid expansion of the affective computing market and the increasing financial stakes for companies integrating these emotional and logical layers.


[Marketsandmarkets](https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/Market-Reports/affective-computing-market-130730395.html) projects the **Global Affective Computing market to grow** from $28.6 billion in 2020 to $136.2 billion by 2026.


It is expected to reach $1,191.6 billion by 2034. This indicates that businesses failing to adopt empathetic interfaces now risk losing share in a trillion-dollar shift toward human-centric AI.


### What industries benefit most from empathetic data retrieval?


Telehealth and high-touch financial services gain the most immediate utility from connecting EVI to private data silos via MCP.


In a clinical setting, an agent using Gemini 4 Carbon can retrieve a patient’s historical treatment adherence from an EHR while simultaneously detecting vocal signs of distress.


In debt collection or insurance adjustments, the agent can cross-reference policy limits in real-time while adjusting its tone to de-escalate conflict. This reduces the liability of human error during high-stress negotiations.
